study type: cohort study (secondary analysis of birth registry data)
outcome: moderately to late preterm birth (32 to <37 weeks of gestation)
very/extreme preterm birth (<32 weeks of gestation)
cohort: The study included 44,117 women who gave birth to singletons between 2000-2015 at the KCMC zonal referral hospital in Moshi Municipality, Kilimanjaro region, northern Tanzania.
finding: The overall proportion of preterm births among singletons was 11.7%, with rising trends between 2000-2015, and various maternal and pregnancy-related factors such as inadequate ANC visits, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, and low birth weight were significant predictors of moderately to late and very/extremely preterm birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean section delivery was associated with higher odds of moderately to late preterm birth (OR=1.16) but showed no statistically significant association with very/extremely preterm birth.
birth_weight: Mentioned as a predictor: Low birth weight (LBW) babies showed extremely higher odds of very/extreme preterm birth (OR=38.34) and moderately to late preterm birth (OR=8.08).
gest_age: All gestational ages were considered, with outcomes specifically defined as moderately to late preterm birth (32 to <37 weeks) and very/extreme preterm birth (<32 weeks).
